subject: history_social
passage: In the dry regions of western India, communities once built stepwells: deep stone structures in which long flights of stairs lead down to the water. Some of these wells were far more than practical sources of water; they were elaborately decorated works of art. ______ Rani ki Vav in Patan, Gujarat, built in the eleventh century, has walls lined with hundreds of carved stone figures arranged along its descending levels.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim: some stepwells "were elaborately decorated works of art." The last sentence describes one particular stepwell with hundreds of carved figures, which illustrates that claim. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "For example" introduces Rani ki Vav as a specific case of a decorated stepwell.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Rani ki Vav agrees with the claim about decorated wells; it does not contrast with it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The carvings at Rani ki Vav are not caused by the fact that some stepwells were decorated; they are an instance of it. This is a tempting trap because the two ideas are closely connected.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Even so" signals something true despite the previous point, but the last sentence supports the previous point.

checks.note: Best fit on the text alone.
